The Prepare-Now Care Roadmap Checklist

What to organize, talk over and keep an eye on while Mom is well.

Download PDF

Mom is well. One of you wants to start touring places, one of you would rather not talk about it, and you'd like something useful to do in between. These are the things worth organizing and talking over while there is no date on anything. Take them in any order. Check what you've done. Anything unchecked is something that hasn't come up yet, and that is all it is.

Organize

Talk over

Keep an eye on

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you organize, talk and keep an eye on things. It doesn't say where Mom should live, when anything should change, who has to do what, or what a change in her days would mean. Nothing on it adds up to a score. A page with every box checked is still preparation, with every decision left where it was.

Ready for the next step?

You've seen what's worth organizing and talking over now, and nothing has been decided for Mom. The care interview adds the picture the plan rests on: it walks you through her situation as it is today, area by area, so the family has something to compare against when it looks again, and turns your answers into a Family Care Profile you can bring to any care conversation.

Where this comes from

Items marked 1 follow AARP's planning guide for families, which starts from the wishes of the person the plan is about and asks each person what they'd prefer to take on. Items marked 2 follow the Family Caregiver Alliance's advice to meet again regularly, and when the situation changes. The rest come from the Family Care Roadmap's own working list for this step.

  1. AARP, Prepare to Care: A Planning Guide for Families
  2. Family Caregiver Alliance, Holding a Family Meeting
